items.stem: A test is 99% accurate for a disease affecting 1 in 1000 people. A random positive is most likely to be:

options.text: A false positive, because the base rate is very low
options.rationale: Correct: with a rare condition, false positives can outnumber true positives.

options.text: A true positive, because the test is 99% accurate
options.rationale: Accuracy alone ignores the low base rate.

options.text: Impossible to reason about without more tests
options.rationale: Bayes' theorem lets us reason with the given numbers.
The low prior makes false positives more likely here.

items.explanation: Correct: with a rare condition, false positives can outnumber true positives.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about a 95% confidence interval are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: It is built by a procedure that captures the true value 95% of the time over repeated samples
options.rationale: Correct: the guarantee is about the long-run procedure.

options.text: A wider interval reflects more uncertainty in the estimate
options.rationale: Correct: width grows with variance and shrinks with sample size.

options.text: There is a 95% probability the true parameter lies in this particular interval
options.rationale: The parameter is fixed; the probability statement is about the procedure.

options.text: It guarantees the sample mean equals the population mean
options.rationale: It does not; it quantifies uncertainty around the estimate.

items.explanation: Correct: the guarantee is about the long-run procedure.

items.stem: A study reports p = 0.001. What does this most directly indicate?

options.text: The data are unlikely under the null hypothesis; it does not by itself show a large effect
options.rationale: Correct: a small p-value concerns surprise under the null, not effect size.

options.text: The effect is large and important
options.rationale: p-values do not measure effect size or importance.

options.text: The result will replicate for certain
options.rationale: A single p-value does not guarantee replication.

options.text: The null hypothesis is proven false
options.rationale: Hypothesis tests give evidence, not proof.

items.explanation: Correct: a small p-value concerns surprise under the null, not effect size.
